Game has a good story, good characters and character development and surprisingly good voice acting.  I would recommend it if you're a fan of RPG's where you control a unique party with lots of neat abilities.
TLDR: Overall Review Score:  8/10
Story 8/10 - Was good and engaging, I wanted to learn more during the entire game right up until the end.

Character Development 8/10 - Also good, lots of variety of skills available and you can mix and match pretty much infinitely to come up with some great combos. All of the characters had a unique backstory and were well developed.  The voices for all the characters was 10/10
Questing & Adventuring - 7/10 - I liked the quests and adventuring, but I ended up with 100's of items I had no idea what to do with.  I assume that means I didn't find all the parts required to put them together into whatever item they were supposed to turn into?  I'm not sure, there wasn't much description around it or directions on what to do with them.
Graphics - 10/10  - The graphics were great, very detailed world, excellently crafted.
Party Gameplay - 10/10 - I really liked this aspect of the game.  My characters were extremely strong, which I appreciated.  I was able to brute force my way through most things just using my party, which for me is great because I'm not huge into RTS.  This could be a good or bad thing, depending on which style of play you prefer.
RTS Gameplay - 7/10 -  It was decent.  My biggest complaint would be the catapult range.  Once the enemy started using them, they could nuke a base from way outside of any tower range, they also immediately disengaged and kited your guys into enemy territory.  I think they need to have less range, and be wayyyyyy slower.  Other then that, there was lots of upgrades, base building, etc. all of which was pretty well done.
Control - 8/10  - I used the WASD configuration, which I thought was good as can be, it meant I had to manually click spells and target, but I liked the manouverability of the camera.  My only complaint was the camera getting stuck on things in high or low terrain areas.
***Bugs*** - I ran into several bugs which stopped me from completing quests.  One was even a show stopper as far as getting my guy stuck in a conversation and then being unable to exit the map.  I got really lucky and found an NPC in a cage to talk too to get myself unstuck. Any bug that I did encounter was patched within a day or two of running into it, so new players probably won't have any issues - but all of this should have been resolved pre-release via testing.
Love:
RTS part feels a bit lacking but RPG part is definitely great. Good writing and cool characters with nicely done loot.

How in Tiara's name does this game have "Mixed" reviews? I am almost 18 hours in and absolutely loving it. Here is my review.
TLDR version: An outstanding game with gorgeous visuals, mixing both RTS and RPG elements into a single game, although I enjoyed the RTS elements more than I enjoyed the RPG ones, but this is preference.
In SpellForce 3, you assume the role of a Corporal in the Royal Army. As such, you practice taking command of troops (RTS element) as you advance in the game. The game has a similar format to other RTS, in the sense that as you progress in the campaign, you unlock higher and higher "tiers" of manpower and equipment. Over the course of the game, you get to command different factions with their own arrays of styles and abilities.
I certainly don't mean to downplay the RPG aspects of the game - they are present and have great depth. You are able to fully equip your "Hero Party" which is your main character and his/her companions. You will also advance them along three main skill trees while assigning attribute points. Each character has their own storyline and set of skills/abilities, and I personally found it fascinating while interacting with them, both in and out of battle.
In writing this, I was trying analyze exactly how they got this game right even while combining RPG and RTS elements. My conclusion is that they did not rush through the development of either parts of the game. Both aspects are fleshed out well and to the perfect depth so as to prevent the player from getting too "bogged down" in either. As I said, the visuals are excellent and the voice acting is spectacular. I mean, they got voice actors for every character, and good ones at that! Another way they were able to really get the combination right is by allowing you to take your Hero party into RTS battles, assigning them to teams if you desire. For instance, the way I play, I assign two heroes to two main battalions in my army, thus giving the troops support with their specialized abilities. I will often use those two battalions for different functions, and will assign smaller platoons, if you will, for other tasks such as guarding outposts, etc.
It boggles my mind that I bought this game for $45. There are AAA games out there which are downright atrocious and can't even measure up to being even HALF as good as this game. It's a shame that this hasn't gotten more publicity. My recommendation: Buy this game and try it out, you will not be disappointed.

You can't divorce a game from the antics of its creator and 'bob's game' is no different.
Years ago a developer threw what was best described as a webcam temper tantrum because Nintendo wouldn't publish his "awesome game."
This is his awesome game: a hodge-podge of other people's designs and work thrown together with horrible looking background art, no real point, and outright Copyright Infringement where bob points out exactly what game he's stealing from in the UI.
Not only that, his supposed one true creation, tetrad, is just a shameless rip-off of the Japanese DS game Trioncube.  I'm guessing bob had a flash cart and didn't think other people played this game in the US.
It was a waste of time back in 2007 when he was pretending to kill himself in front of a webcamera and holding "protests" at Nintendo stores that confused employees more than anything, and it's a waste of time now.  This is a sub-Flash level game and you can find plenty of similar Tetris/Puzzle Fight/Puyo Pop clones on Facebook that actually give you something more than just a high score when you finish.

I bought this game for somewhere around a dollar with the expectancy that it would be a bad game, and boy did it deliver.
The game may have been published in 2006, but really that doesn't excuse the poor quality at all.
The game is insanely prone to crashes. If you skip the opening credits to the game, it crashes. If you minimize the game, it crashes. If you try to bring up steam or xsplit overlay in the game, it crashes. When loading or starting a game, there is a 50-50 chance the game will crash. Same with when you die in the game.
Modeling in the game is extremely lazy. All characters I have seen have been one of about 5 variants.
The AI is awful as well. Enemies will be standing about 5 feet away from a firefight and not notice. Enemies will rush you for no real reason.

So I’m kind of on a Batman high after playing Batman -The TellTale Series, so I bought Arkham Asylum and Arkham City during the Summer Sale. Played Arkham City first, because that’s the better game of the two, and I went nuts trying to finish all of the Riddler @^*% in Story Mode- THERE’S SO MUCH @^*% TO COLLECT. After Arkham City was revealed people got excited to play the sequel to the best Batman game at the time, Arkham Asylum. I wasn’t exactly all aboard the hype train during this time because I wasn’t formally introduced to the Arkham Series until I discovered SomeCallMeJohnny sometime in 2012. I didn’t get my own Xbox 360 until that Christmas nor the actual games some months later. When I finally did I fell in love with both games, even Arkham Asylum despite it’s shortcomings compared to its sequel. Arkham City expanded upon everything from the first game and received such great critical reception that it was made Game of the Year. But enough of me sucking this game’s♥♥♥♥♥♥ let’s get to the review.
Dave Rides The Steam Train To… Batman: Arkham City
After the events of the previous game former Warden of Arkham Asylum, Quincy Sharp, ran for Mayor of Gotham City and won. With his newfound power he took an entire section of the city and converted it into a prison. Naturally this sparked much controversy with the citizens of Gotham, many of who I swear must’ve been made homeless because of this whole mess, leading to a coalition of people demanding for the demolishment of Arkham City. Bruce Wayne holds a press conference to promote the prison’s destruction, but not long after its start Wayne is arrested and thrown into the prison (which is rather convenient for the people who take him into custody because he held the conference right outside the prison like a dumb@$$). There he’s greeted by Hugo Strange, the man in charge of Arkham City, who is fully aware that Bruce Wayne is the Batman. Strange threatens that if Bruce tries to stop him he will reveal Batman’s identity to the world. DON’T WORRY!!! (I’m going to spoil this here) Despite you predictably going off to stop Strange, he NEVER tells anybody who Batman is under the mask. Even though he has his outing in Arkham Knight anyway… WTF? Either way, Wayne is released into Arkham City, calls for a drop off Batsuit, suits up and glides off to adventure.
Not much changes in gameplay from Arkham Asylum aside from some new BatToys to play with. Practically everything from last time returns here, the only things really missing are Multi-Batarangs and tracing the alcohol from someone’s breath. You still have one attack button and one counter button, however with some upgrades you can improve the flow of combat to be even faster, so you can pretty much button mash through each fight with high combo ratings. The rest of the controls are simple, making it easy for anyone to just pick up and play, but difficult to master (I love games like that). If you’re ever lost on who these characters are or just what the $&#* is going on, you can unlock character bios and stories to help fill in details you might be confused about. Other than the main story there are side-quests you can pursue if you feel up to it, or just to stop them from bothering you: like Victor Zsasz who calls various payphones throughout Arkham City, and if you don’t pick up he’ll kill a man; Deadshot, “the world’s most ACCURATE assassin”, murdering random prisoner’s incarcerated in the prison; random corpses lying around with their faces sliced off; hunt down containers holding the TITAN substance from Arkham Asylum; collect various trophies and solves conundrums by the Riddler, which takes way to $&#**^% long; or hunt down this Mysterious Watcher from the Order of Saint Dumbass.
I don’t know if this because of my desktop was lacking in proper specs, but I noticed many times that when in Detective Mode, mooks majorly unseeable and would only appear at certain sections of the game or at certain angles. This never happened to me when I owned the game on the 360. Not only that but sometimes the counter prompt would not appear at all! Causing me to fall to my death one too many times. Hey, at least I was able to play this game with my plug-in 360 controller…
RANT TIME - Catwoman. I $&#**^% hate her and she has no business being in this game except fan service. Whelp, sorry to disappoint to Rocksteady but I’m not popping any boners. If you have choice of purchasing the Catwoman Add-On DLC… DON’T BUY IT. She has no major impact on the story of the game and her own little feline antics do not provide any motivation to continue to play as her. I don’t want to play as this #&^% (03-21-14-20), I wanna be the middle-aged man dressed in bat-themed spandex!
So the game obviously isn’t perfect, but I feel its faults are overweight by its strengths. Arkham City has become a classic in the Batman mythos and is just as great as The Animated Series or The Dark Knight. If you enjoyed the last game or if you just enjoy Batman in general, pick up Arkham City and give it a spin, I’m sure you’ll enjoy it. Just make sure you got the alternate costume pack for Batman, looking at his default costume makes me sad. (I personally love the Batman Beyond costume, remember what Edna said “no caps!”.)

I'm giving this a thumbs-up but there are definitely things you should be forewarned about. The game is incredibly short and ends on a "to be continued". Boo. There are only a few music scores that are all repeated but I guess, considering the game length, that's not a huge deal. There's also no map and no hints as to where to go next. There ARE hints during hidden object scenes and a skip button for puzzles however. I should mention that I never got stuck for long, I never used any hints in HO areas, and I didn't skip any puzzles.
Now for the reasons I'm recommending this. It's chock-full of hidden object scenes. In fact, that's the main reason to play it. And they're good old fashioned HO scenes - lots to find and no having to make extra moves before collecting your items. I know developers now add a bunch of twists and extra features to their hidden object scenes to liven it up but, really, I found NOT having to do all that very refreshing. The objects are all fair as well. You might have to search a bit to find them but they're all right there - not hiding behind anything, not mislabled, and not making you click all over for it to register. Again, refreshing!
Add to that an interesting and twisted story and some lovely graphics and character models. Puzzles aren't going to make you tear your hair out and it's easy to figure out where to use your collected items.
I certainly wish it had been longer and..... just be prepared for an unsatisfying ending. But if you want to relax and just find a bunch of items, try this game out. Just make sure to get it when it's on sale or in a bundle.

Oh my god, I'm in love with this game.  Let's try to keep it short and sweet:
Pros:
-Gameplay. OH MY GOD the gameplay. The game is incredible open and flexible in how you approach objectives. The game encourages exploration and experimentation. I can't stress it enough: It's a great, great stealth game.
-Artstyle (not to be confused with graphics). Even though it can be generic in places (like human designs) it's absolutely fantastic in other departments (like level design). Overall, I really enjoyed my time in this world.
-Story starts up confusing, but have a nice twist, so it's quite enjoyable in the end.
Cons:
-Texture quality is low, so the game doesn’t look good up close
-Animations could use some polish, especially in cutscenes
-Some minor gameplay inconveniences (like how you cant turn corners while drabbing the ledge)
-There few instances where the game funneled me into places that were borderline unfair and required quicksave scumming. Fortunately, there were very few.
-Some bugs, although very minor in my experience
-Some people don't like that the game recycle maps (each one is used twice). I don't mind it, as you experience them in different ways (different point of entry and exit, different guard positions,  objectives)
Overall, I enjoy the game immensely. Actually, I simply don't want it to end, and am replaying previous levels to collect everything, and to enjoy the game again with my acquired skills (both in game and player-side). I think that it's the best praise that I can give to a game - I like it so much I don't want it to end.

This review was last edited when I had completed the "Parachute Landing" Challenge (8/18)
SimpleRockets is a 2D rocket simulation with easy to use controls, basic but adequate graphics. You can either take on a preset challenge or fly in a sandbox environment. You design your own rocket from preset modules and then fly it! I found the game tremendous fun to play as well as educational on some of the basic principals of flying rockets
The build screen is a drag and drop affair where modules are dropped onto attach points. There are no resource restrictions so the design of your rocket is limited only by the modules available and your imagination.
The flight screen is a 2D display of your rocket. You control your rocket by using a segmented bar to select the amount of thrust and a circular slider to select the direction. There is an "action" button to allow you to perform acts like ignite rockets and separate modules. The flight screen can be split in two to also display a map showing your current flight path. The amount of fuel you have remaining is displayed as a progress bar.
The game plays in full screen or windows mode (although with restricted resolutions) and has a pause button, essential if like me you have a young family who can interupt you at any time! Input is via a mouse.
There is a good tutorial which takes 5-10 minutes and gave me a good basic understanding of what the game was about.
Once you have completed the tutorials there are 18 challenges to take on ranging from a simple blast off procedure through reaching a planetary orbit to landing on a moon. Typically a single attempt at a challenge is less than 5 minutes.
However, this is the type of game that you need to be a gaming/physics genius to suceed first time on many of the challenges. So be prepared for disaster again and again and again until you find the right design along with the right strategy to succeed. The knock on consequence is that a 5 minute attempt becomes an hour to actually succeed ..
There is a personal high score table for challenges so you can compare your scores with different designs/strategies and try to keep improving your personal best
There is also a Sandbox mode where you can pick a planet to build and test your rocket on. The planets are based on our own solar system.

More In-Depth Review:
Nidhogg is a brilliant game in which two players fight each other to reach the end of the map. You have to actually think about what you are going to do, because just rushing to the other person and attempting to stab them rarely works. This game was meant for you to actually be swordfighting each other by parrying the enemy sword, trying to knock the sword out of their hands, tripping them, stabbing  them if they don't block with their sword, catching them off guard, kicking them from the air, rolling behind them, or even throwing your sword at them. And even if you don't have a sword, you can still kick, punch, and trip the enemy. There are 4 different maps to play on, with each having different strategies you can use, as well as amazing artwork and music. The singleplayer mode is incredibly fun and can be very challenging, but the AIs are not the smartest, and almost all of them will fall for somewhat simple tricks, allowing you to kill them very easily, unless they get lucky or you mess up. Completing singleplayer typically takes me about 30-45 minutes. The online multiplayer community is dead, and you will be more likely to win the lottery than find someone in matchmaking. Local multiplayer is very fun. You can choose which map to play on, create custom settings such as always jumping, no swords, rainbow trails, always crouching, and more. This game is made for local multiplayer! Do not be disappointed and give bad reviews because you can't find anyone online to play against. When you do find a match, I have never experienced any lag or glitches. 10/10

TLDR;
While the story is lacking, the mechanics are decent enough that I would recommend this if you get it for < $5. I would not pay $15 for this game because it lacks long term replayability that you can find in games like Banished.
Now for those of you who don't mind reading.....
My mom and I each picked this game up when it was on sale and it was definitely a good buy for the price we paid.
We love Banished and while I can say that this does not have the replayability of Banished (in my opinion I could see MAYBE playing it through two or three times, whereas Banished has much much more replayability), it did entertain me for an evening or two.
The crafting system is simple, click what raw materials you want or let the auto production go crazy, I ended up doing a bit of both. For more refined products, you could only click to add more.
You get to make 3 interconnected colonies on 3 different planets/moons. I liked how they were interconnected crafting-wise, however I wish the stories had also been connected in some way.
I thought the story would be a bit lengthier than it was, but it was decent. Each colony had a different story line
I found Mar's story to be the most fleshed out, however the dialogue and VO is a bit... unnatural. Ceres' story was shorter and shallower but the dialogue flowed better than on Mars. The last planet had a SUPER short story and seemed to be the most "important" one scientifically but because of the VO it seemed more like a pat on the back instead of a true celebration of the achivement you supposedly make.

There is a sandbox mode and a survival mode. The defense mechanics in the game aren't quite fleshed out enough to be compelling for a survival mode. The sandbox mode has possible replayability, however I never ended up playing the sandbox mode since it is exactly the same as story mode, except there are no objectives or story.

With respect to single player:  This is an interesting game if you enjoy settlement management games.  The game has many buildings that each provide different base resources, as well as, more advanced fabricatable items.  To balance the colony well, the production of these different elements must be carefully monitored.  It is possible to set each to automatically produce given resources, however, this will quickly overwhelm your storage, so it is best to manually control the production.  The sandbox aspect of the game allows for new players to get practice with the different buildings in order to better understand their capabilities.  When playing in other modes it is possible to esstablish trade across planets.  For those familar with other settlement games, while this game does have multiple buildings, it does not have the depth found in games like civilization at this point, which allows multiple cities, or the depth of construction found with sim city.  The game does not appear to be being updated frequently, so it is unclear at this point if additional updates will continue in the future.  As a finished games, this is worth playing, if it continues to be developed, then it has a lot of potential.  That being said, the game is quite interesting and worth purchasing, especially when on sale.  All in all, I recommend adding this game to your collection if you enjoy settlement management games.

Let me expound a bit...
This almost seems like someone had an idea for a decent Tapping Game on a mobile platform and then decided to turn it into a bare-bones PC port.  This game, so far, seems to be nothing more than clicks.  Want to make resources?  Click to make one of ANYTHING, but you only get one per click, so if you want 40, click 40 times.  Or you can just turn on automation and it will keep making things ad infinitum.  There's no "process" to make anything.  It's just clicks.  You don't have to send out astronauts to mine ore, you don't have to extract anything from the soil.  Well, maybe you do theoretically, but if you want to go that route, it's all in your imagination.
Want to build the more complicated buildings?  Just wait til the automated counters tick up and build one when you have enough supplies.
I'm renaming this Earth Space Colonies: Click and Wait.

Many basic game concepts have not implemented yet, and the players time quickly devolves into an unsustainable amount of micro-management. There's a strong imbalance between what the player must do manually and what is automated behind the scenes. For example:
- When building habitation structures, new colonists instantaneously fill the structures regardless of whether or not the colony even has the ability to accept deliveries (extreme and illogical automation)
- To construct a new building or object - of which there are many - each unit of material required for construction has to be manually produced by the player (extreme and illogical micromanagement).
I hope development continues on this project. It has the foundation to go far.

If My Heart Had Wings is an incredibly emotional visual novel featuring both soaring highs and plummeting lows. The story focusses on Aoi Minase and the Soaring club and how they  cope with loss and love whilst sharing their passion and dreams together.
When reading this novel you will easily become attached to the characters sharing in their plight, hope and dreams. There are 5 routes with the members of the soaring club that you can take Kotori's, Ageha's, Amane's, Asa's and Yoru's each character has their own different backstory and personality that will both charm and entice you into playing their storylines, leading to a rich rewarding experience upon completion of the storyline.
The artwork is also crisp using a vast and beautiful array of colours providing awe inspiring scenes and capturing moments perfectly. Characters both main and side are also well drawn, with a large assortment of sprites each with their own distinguishable characteristics (less distinguishable for the twins). The soundtrack is also composed well and enhances the mood and emotions within scenes, comedic for humour, inspiring for uplifting scenes and sombre for sadder scenes, providing an enthralling rich experience for the reader.
Writing whilst beautiful and poetic at times is the only place where i can find negatives for this visual novel. Translation of this novel has led to mistranslation of some words so Engrish is present, within this novel however outside of one storyline it doesn't affect the readers experience that much. Also due to cutting of scenes to make this novel all ages some words have being swapped, you will notice these and either find them frustrating or charming and funny like i did, however outside of this there aren't any real problems with this visual novel.
In conclusion If My Heart Had Wings is not just a visual novel it's an experience that is both rich and rewarding, i would recommend this game to those who are both new and already familiar to visual novels as it provides good value (over 30 hours of gameplay with scene skipping) and a rewarding experience that you won't soon forget. 8.5/10

I am going to review this as a VISUAL NOVEL, not a game. I've seen a lot of people make this mistake. They review visual novels as a video game with gameplay and etc etc. Note that this is going to be a casual review not a serious one. This is my first review that I have done. Enjoy
Review:
Okay. The story starts off with our protagonist, Aoi, going back to his hometown because of his injury during a cycling race. As Aoi is walking through his hometown he meets a girl in a wheelchair named Kotori. Her wheelchair is flat and Aoi fixes it etc etc. Lets keep moving on because I want to finish this ASAP. Aoi arrives at a dorm which he is going to live called "Flying Fish Manor" little did he know that it was a girl's dorm. Kotori also lives in the dorm. (Opinion time!!): Ok, when I first saw him entering the girl's dorm, the first thing that came on my mind is "Awww crap. He's gonna get a harem". (Opinion time ends). Aoi goes back to school and meets his childhood friend, Ageha. They catch up etc etc. Aoi stumbles across a garage which is actually the "Soaring Club". The Soaring Club only has one member which is Amane. Kotori, Ageha and Aoi joins the Soaring Club to fulfill a dream which is to soar the skies and to see the morning glory clouds.
I really like the characters compared to other REALLY good visual novel characters. They have full voice acting, extremely well designed. Each character has a role and isn't there just to fill up the void. The characters each have a unique personality.
Kotori Habane: Strong willed, confident. Sometimes a cry baby
Ageha Himegi: Typical tomboy (A really cute one as well)
Amane Mochizuki: An airheaded, super genius, super repeat student.
Asa Kazato: A bright, warm girl. Clumsy and a bit airheaded.
Yoru Kazato: Yoru is Asa's twin. Her personality is complete opposite from her sister's. She is also attached to her sister.
Lets talk about the art first. The art is ABSOLUTELY AMAZING. nuff said... Now the sounds. The music/sounds is composed really well. Well enough to make you want to play more of this visual novel. The music/sounds fit the events that occur and at some points sound really soothing.
I just noticed how much time I spent on this review. Haha. The visual novel overall is amazing! Nice characters, great art/sounds, really good story. It tells you a lot of information about gliders as well!! There was only a few bad points about this game which is mainly the translation of the visual novel. As you progress through the visual novels you will notice the typos. The visual novel will provide you 20-30 hours of gameplay (reading), a few choices, 5 girls to choose from which is definitely worth the price which is 15 dollars. Especially when it can give you a free ticket to the feels train. I really enjoyed this visual novel and hoping to see more from MoeNovel. So if you like romance, slice of life visual novels. I definitely recommend this visual novel to you!!

This game is dated as it is from early 2000 techno, perhaps earlier. It feels like a cheap Half Life but with crappier animations and worse sound effects.

The art style is typical East-European \ Russian in the sense that the colors-scheme's are sober and not Disney-like. The best part though is the objects in the game. They actually feel authentic for that time (1940's). White plates and cups were common objects then and are in the game, simple chairs, locking mechanics. It all adds up to a authentic feeling.
Gameplay itself is like a corridor shooter. On easy you can walk up to a guy and shoot him in the face without much getting much damage yourself, which is a bit too easy. Weapons feel ok but not great. All in all a game you need to want to play, be it just for the style.
Recommended therefore just for the authenticity, for great gameplay load up something else.

Finding Paradise is a part adventure, part visual novel videogame developed by Freebird Games. It's the sequel to their previous effort, To the Moon, and the second game in a supposed series. Once again the player takes control of two scientists, dr. Eva Rosalene and dr. Neil Watts, employees of a fictional Sigmund Corporation, as they use the technology at their disposal to help a dying man, Colin, achieve happiness by exploring his memories and change them as needed.
Since the game could be considered a direct follow-up to To the Moon, Finding Paradise offers the player the same gameplay as its predecessor. You are basically tasked to visit different memory locations, find all the points of interest and then solve a rather simple, grid-based puzzle mini-game: so once again the core gameplay should be considered just a vehicle for its story, which is arguably the game's main attraction.
Once again the developers have made a super use of the RPG Maker assets: the environments look absolutely stunning and detailed for this kind of game, the sprites' animations are most of the time incredibly convincing and every once in a while the gameplay will suddendly change, often in humorous and surprising ways which are totally unexpected (in a good way).
When it comes to story, Finding Paradise the same quality featured in the original game, and maybe it even surpasses it. The whole game is really a very touching tale about the true meaning of happiness and the role of regrets and mistakes in our live: heavy subjects that the developers managed to take on in a very tasteful manner.
Given the very low price of the game and the kind of experience you are going to get for yourself I can't see any reason not to reccomend Finding Paradise to anyone

What would've happened if Killing Floor had zombies instead of mutants?
Okay, I partially lied, as game represents some kind of a mixture between "Killing Floor" and "Left For Dead".
Gameplay itself is somewhat close to "Left for dead" - a team of five players has to achieve some goal (at the moment it's only blow up the target and successfully leave the map). However there are classes with special abilities available. For example support class can spawn a crate for refilling ammunition/hp/armor. Specialist class can spawn turret, etc etc etc.
At specific moments game suddenly changes and forces players to go defensive mode (e.g. gates are slowly opening, so players can't rush any longer, insane amount of zombies is spawned and some spooky music is played).
That sums up my gameplay experience. Even though my experience is quite short I don't actually think that game would bring me any more surprises. So, as you can see, concept itself is quite appealing (at least for me), but there's some critics to a game at it's current state:
-Too few zombie classes (slow weak, fast weak, slow strong).
-Too few weapons (I mean sorry guys but we are in 2015, 2 weapons per class is just too few. Why won't you make several weapons per class, accessible through spawn menu).
-Lack of logic. And I believe this deserves some elaboration:
*Maps don't have descrpition. Who are we? Why are there zombies? Why should we blow up the target?
*Weapons have weird classification. We play as some kind of USA troops but one of the classes have Galil? Why would USA troops use galil if they have own guns, like M4 and so on? Or do we represent international unit? So there's working aviation? In this case why sending a squad when you can send an airstrike?
*classes can be abused. For example you can take several supports and make up improvised barricade (near doors, for example), making AI just helplessly stand and ignore you, waiting to be killed. Maybe forcing players 'unpack' the turret ammobox for couple of seconds would partially fix the issue, who knows...
-Map quality. While I really like the models (zombies, soldiers, weapons, etc), I feel like maps should still have huge work on decorations etc. At the moment they just look empty and low quality. I wouldn't say anything if project carried 'alpha stage' status, but it's on beta stage already, hence why I'm mentioning this (yes, all of the games I played on beta stage had maps at decent level). Speaking of maps, there's quite small amount of maps to play at the moment.
-Weapon physics. Not gonna lie, as I didn't test ALL the weapons, but support's SMG is pretty easy to control, just crouch, aim via RMB and spray. It would shoot slightly above the aim.
As I said, Can't tell for all weapons, but I assume other weapons are pretty similar in a matter of handling.
-Game is pretty much unballanced. Some classes' weapons are useless comparing to melee attack (which insta-kills any weak zombie). I'm pretty sure if I put some training, I'll be able to complete whole map using knife only.
Would I recommend this game? Maybe, but not at it's current development stage... Let's say it has potential and if done properly, it might become an F2P version of L4D.
Who would I recommend that game to at it's current state? I don't know really. No offense to the developer, but I can name way better games about zombies, worth their attention.
But yeah, speaking of recommendations... I guess it'd be people who have desperate wish to play coop with their friends but don't wish to pay for L4D...
I'll make one more review later when game is done, to see what've changed. I really hope to see some great changes. By now, unfortunately, I place 'dislike' button, even though game is still under development.
Game is free anyway, so feel free to test it by yourself and give your opinions.
It's not as good as L4D2, but it's free.

Gunpoint is a stealth/puzzle game with very unique mechanics and gameplay. Fans of pixel art will be drawn to this rich cyberpunk setting, and practically anyone who enjoys strategic stealth games will enjoy Gunpoint as well. The main mechanics, Bullfrog (climb walls, leap with force that smashes windows and knocks out guards) and Crosslink (link two electrical items together like a light switch and a locked door so that activating one also activates the other) creates gameplay that will differ a lot to other games of this genre. Also the music is nice to listen to as well.
There is a story in this game, nothing fantastic, but it is interesting and relatively immersive. You will get dialogue options that are actually impactful at times, but usually you have the option to reply seriously or jokingly. Another thing that's interesting about this game are the achievements. You'll get what I mean when you get the game.
The autosave system is pretty flawed, either taking you back exactly at the point where you died or about a minute and a half beforehand. Also there is quite a limited choice in how you approach things; ultimately the level can only be done one way. However, it's still a good game and worth a buy.

While I would recommend playing Of Orcs and Men first, it is a very different game.  Plotwise Styx has some twists that add to what is learned from Of Orcs and Men but overall you can play it without it.
Steathing at its finest.  You get a basic toolset, a target on your map, and no direction aside from that.  Every new room or area gives you a new puzzle.  Do you find away around through a tunnel or climb up a wall?  Kill the civilian or the guard first?  Some enemies can only be defeated by poisoning or goblin traps.  F5 and F9 get used frequently.
Steath is also interesting because you can get caught in the shadows.  Different enemy types can see you differently as well.  One type can't see you but it can hear your footsteps and another can just sense your presense.  It creates new puzzles for which way you approach the areas.  Getting caught isn't too bad as you can quickly parry to kill but it's better to just reload.
To add some challenge to each level there are several side objects like not being seen, not killing anyone, and picking up coins.
On to the bad.  Like Of Orcs and Men, it's fairly clear this was made by a small team with a smaller budget.  While there are more animated cinematics than in Of Orcs and Men, there are still a lot of painted animatics.  It works to play out the plot though with what happens.
The biggest problem that a lot of people have is that a LOT of levels are recycled.  The idea is that you need to go through this huge castle so of course you might pass through the lab a few times.  They vary it up with new enemy placements and different lighting (less places to hide).  I would have said reduce the backtracking and trim the story down.  The upside, more instances to sneak and kill.

Styx is an extremely enjoyable, difficult, and rewarding Stealth game that I consider one of the greatest I've ever played in the genre. It has a great story, compelling and unique gameplay, a protagonist who isnt a morally righteous busybody, and a very nice artstyle. From beginning to end this adventure held my attention firmly and kept me coming back for more. I definitely would recommend this game to anyone who wants a game like I describe.

Styx: MoS follows Styx, a goblin assassin with almost total amnesia beyond the ability to remember that his name is indeed Styx. Styx must navigate his way through the dangerous Tower of Akenash guarded by thousands of ruthless humans with a uniform hatred for all things greenskin. His goal is to acquire the heart of the tree that grows within the tower, the source of the ingame
, Amber.
Styx is in my opinion a masterpiece of the stealth genre, it is a game that I have desired to play for many years. This game nails many essential elements to any great stealth game and brings more to the table. This game is not only rewarding but challenging, something missing from alot of new stealth games. You always have to be on lookout for guards, secret passages, areas to climb, ways to outmanuvere and survive your encounters. I personally recommend playing this game on the max difficulty as it really adds to the depth of this game.
As Styx is a angry little goblin, surrounded by angry large humans, he needs to keep to the darkness, on the hardest difficulty even a lowly worker hammering in nails can quickly overpower Styx within seconds and smash his head in with ease. But size isnt everything, and if he gets the drop on you, the tables will quickly turn. This game is not the type of game you should play if you expect any deep sword play, there is parrying below the max difficulty, however it is not anything like Assassin's Creed or the newer Splinter Cell games where you can rely on your combat skills to get yourself out of a situation. If you're caught, you have to run and hide or else you will die simply.
The game has an RPG element to it in that Styx' skills can be upgraded to acquire new techniques that can then be used in the field. From basic things like silent landings, the ability to carry more throwing knives, to things like planting trap's with Styx's imperfect clone, or dive onto enemies from above for aerial kills. Styx has a variety of capabilities in his arsenal. With amber he can create a imperfect clone of himself, see in the dark, and turn invisible for a short while. He can throw daggers, whistle, and of course stab his enemies in a large variety of ways and whistle to collect people's attention.
There is also a parkour element which is easy to learn but difficult to master, however when you have figured it out Styx becomes a acrobatic wunderkind and can soar down 50 foot chasms onto ledges at your whimsy without taking a scratch. Enemies slowly become more difficult as you go along and the game allows you to proceed with a Non Lethal route if you so desire. It rewards you with skill points after each mission depending on how well you did and grades you on things such as how much were spotted, bodies were discovered, etc. I wouldn't worry about this though if this can get to you. It is much more enjoyable for a first playthrough to just play the way you think Styx would.

Styx' graphics are pretty good in my opinion, landscapes can be very visually appealing although I feel the game does not have enough anti aliasing for some reason. Styx' character model is very nice looking and the enemy designs are also quite appealing.
I primarily play games for the story, this is mostly a curse as I cannot enjoy games lacking in a decent narrative. Styx I felt delivered on it's plot and delivers a satisfying beginning middle and end. Very similar to a Coming of Age story is how I would describe it. Cutscenes are beautifully drawn and the voice acting is quite good as well, although some human NPC voices can feel a bit overused.
Dishonored: Styx is very very similar to dishonored in many ways. It has a very similar almost steampunk universe, magical powers at the protagonist's disposal, and both have very similar stories. Styx is basically like Dishonored with 3rd Person and more focus on Stealth.
Assassin's Creed: Parkour elements like Assassin's Creed, larger focus on assassinating in Styx, and no distracting future plot.
I recommend this game if you're a fan of Stealth, this game is amazing and I am glad to hear it is getting a sequel in 2016.

For ~10h you traverse levels  dodging the enemies, and unfortunately, some enemies are quite special, like floating skull heads, elves that can sense your smell. The biggest issue with this game is when you're trying to be completely stealthy you can fall victim to random sounds, especially when killing a guard. The game is most challenging when you go for no kill/no alert, especially if you combine that with gathering all side objectives. Easily one of the best stealth oriented games. The hand to hand combat is clunky, and honestly not rewarding enough to even want to engage in it. The further you advance the more flashy ways you can kill guards, but as I said, if you're still trying for total stealth, sometimes bodies can make a sound when they otherwise would not.
A slightly smaller issue is throughout the entire game I was never given a prompt on how to whistle to gain distract a guard and make him move. At one point there's a loading tip that informs you your clone can do most of the same actions as you can, such as making noise. Looking in the keybinds showed me you can press X to whistle. It's almost essential later on if you're going for a full stealth run.
I found the story to be very captivating and interesting. The climax about halfway through was unexpected and the challenges it brought were just as fun. If you skip cutscenes, you'll miss out on a lot of story and the game will get confusing. I suggest playing through once normally then going back for achievments and insignias.
Definitely recommend this if you enjoy stealth oriented games. The hardest difficulty, plus going for full stealth makes it a fun and challenging game. Beyond that, the special ways to dispatch guards can lend for some fun if you go replay old missions to get missed insignias.

I finished the game in something like 44 hours, but there is replayability to it if you would like to beat all the mission possible objectives.

At the beginning I was disliking the idea of the amber, the clones etc. I remember ironising "how convenient". Highly recommended for any stealth game lover.

Where to begin? How about the thing that is really terrible about this game, the UI.
I start the tutorial which is OK, and at some point it asks me to build a modular habitat. Up until this point I just clicked on various icons and something would drop from orbit. I saw the habitat, but I could not build it. There is no explanation in the tutorial.
So after messing around a bit, I see that I can build a workshop (it is the only thing I can build at this point). So I make it and then try to build a habitat, and I still can't. Then I see that I can hit some automatic build mode thingy, and suddenly the thing starts cranking out a bunch of resources.
After a while I can now build the habitat because I have the basic resources I need. OK, so its just a poor tutorial at this point. So then I am instructed to build a few other things, some of which I can, but then I get stuck again because this workshop has produced a bunch of useless stuff and filled up my inventory.
I then figure out that I need to delete stuff I do not need to make room, but after I figured this out, an earthquake happens and blows up all of my water and oxygen. There is nothing in the tutorial about this. And so I start over after noticing I can turn that off in the options menu.
Anyway here is the gist of why the UI is horrendously bad. So to make some thing, you might need to make 10 iron, 5 glass, 3 wood 6 methane and like 3 gears (which take some amount of iron and titanium each). So you need to make resources for the gears and then make the gears and then make the resources for everything else to plop your building down.
You have to do all this manually mind you. So there is this UI which lets you see all the things you can produce and lets you produce things, but it DOES NOT SHOW YOU how much you actually have. IE: You may know that X thing needs 10 iron, but you can't see how much iron you have from that screen.
Then there is a screen that shows you how much you have, but you can't produce anything from there. Oh, and you can't see the resources you need from any screen but the info screen on the thing you want to build. So you would need to memorize everything and then manually make everything.
If the developer reads this review, you just make to make your UI sane.
I would suggest that the colony produces the resources it needs automatically. IE: I want to build a habitat, then I place the thing down, and it automatically makes everything I need.
You should also combine the build resources screen with the one showing what you have and then you should also add a storage threshold, so I could say, keep a minimum of 10 iron available at all times.
This would go a long way with making your UI much more user friendly. Also please clean up the tutorial, make it show you how to build more complex stuff and certainly go with building maintance and all that. Oh, please use more sensible graphics that fit with the elements they represent. IE: Iron in your UI is a white cube with some tiny dots on it. I would naturally in no way, associate that with iron. How about a stack of iron ingots or steel girders or something that a normal human would look at and think "Iron" instead of "What the heck is that supposed to be?"

I grabbed this game during the Steam summer sale for about three dollars, and it was well worth the price. That's not a compliment - this game is three dollars worth of fun, now at five times the worthy cost.
It might be more fun if there was an online community, but there isn't, or at least there wasn't when I was playing.
Overall it's a decent game. Fairly fun. The basic idea is that you get to flip, jump, and run around like a normal platformer, with the added bonus of having to fence/fist-fight enemies. Once you kill an enemy, you can start running towards the end goal. If an enemy kills you, HE can run towards the end goal. Whoever dies gets to respawn and try to stop the other from getting there, but the guy running can literally jump over you and keep going. It takes a bit of skill and getting used to, but when you pick up the controls and start really understanding things, you'll get the hang of it.
Again, it's a decent game, it's just not worth fifteen dollars. Maybe if there were more people to play online with, or there were more stages, characters, or weapons, but there's only about four or five stages (if even that many), one type of weapon (not counting hand-to-hand), and there's only the one character (you can't even choose your color). So, all in all, it's just not worth it.

Here's a steamed chicken recipe.
you'll need
2 skinless, boneless chicken breast
1 cup salt
2 tablespoons vegetable oil
1 onion, finely chopped
2 cloves garlic, finely chopped
5 tablespoons light soy sauce
2 tablespoons sesame oil
2 sprigs fresh cilantro
Steps:
1
Place chicken and salt in a bowl. Evenly rub salt into chicken. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
2
Rinse chicken and place in a pot fitted with a steamer basket over water. Bring water to a boil, and steam chicken until juices run clear, about 30 minutes.
3
Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat. Stir in onion and cook until tender. Mix in garlic, and cook about 1 minute. Stir in soy sauce and sesame oil, and remove from heat. Scoop over the chicken to serve. Garnish with cilantro.

Writing a review for this game is kind of difficult. The game shines in many aspects and comes short in others and the main problem in rating this game, is that depending on how you like to play the game, the gameplay experience changes.

GAMEPLAY

Let me explain. The game is primarily a stealth game. It does not only count being spotted visually by enemies but making sounds as well as disturbing the environment in some way (putting out lights etc).

In that sense you are playing a very complex 3d puzzle where you have to time your kills and/or movements just right in order to avoid being seen.

With that in mind, it is possible to go through the game without killing anyone (except specific characters required by missions). The enemies are varied and your ways of dispatching them are too. You can poison them, sabotage chandeliers to get them to crush enemies below, sneaking behind enemies and cracking their necks etc. Bodies can be dragged and hidden away so enemies don’t get alerted. This is one of the game’s biggest strengths. Not only do you have a lot of ways to deal with enemies, but there are many physical paths to your goal. This means that depending on how you have spent your talent points, you can end up with a skillset that lets you g through an area much easier than other areas of the map.

There are shortcuts and there are times when you observe guards patrolling in order to time your moves just right. In fact you do that a lot of the time. This is a game that is slower than most and requires some patience. It is immensely rewarding to make it through an area after carefully planning and executing jumps and moving from cover to cover at just the right time.

The enemies are varied and require different strategies to take into account.

Now here is a big negative. The combat system. Left mouse button is overused. You have to press it quickly behind a person to kill them loudly. If you want a muffled kill, you press and hold the same left mouse button. People have mentioned this before and yes the combat system is awful. If a guard discovers you, you enter combat which involves having to press the left mouse button just as they try to hit you to parry their hits. Once you parry three times you press the same button to kill that guard. You cannot damage them and even though there is a swinging animation, if you miss the very tight timing of trying to parry, their hit goes through and you take damage. If the guard was along you might be ok. If he has friends, his friends are also either swinging or throwing knives at you. After a while you realize that when you are caught by 2+ guards you are best to reload a previous save. There is an invisibility skill but it is situational and expensive to use.

If you are going to play this game in full stealth mode and never engage in combat, this game will be awesome for you. If you are going to kill a guard here and there and stealth most of the way, you are still good. You cannot go on a murderous rage however. For a game that gives so much freedom, I found this limiting.

GRAPHICS

The graphics of the game are great. Environments are beautiful and it runs quite well on my aging system.

STORY

The story in this game is told using cartoon cut scenes which are very effective. The main character is actually very well voiced and very likable. I understand this is a prequel so there were a few things that at first were a bit confusing but by the end you get enough info to fill the gaps. This was to me a very strong part of the game.

FINAL GRIPE

The final boss fight is unlike any in the rest of the game. It not only feels out of place in a stealth game, but it has one absolutely horrendous flaw. The area you enter for the final fight has no resources. The problem is that this comes unexpected and you are not told you have to prepare for it. This area in particular lies at the very end of a brutal level where you are using all your potions and knives and everything in your ability just to barely survive. There is no indication that you will not be able to resupply before the final showdown.

The problem is that if you enter the fight low on supplies and possibly health, it is an absolutely brutal and pretty much  impossible fight, where you are literally killed in one shot. A person playing this with full throwing knives and potions can breeze this fight and the difficulty is so variable based on these factors. Without being able to resupply you are basically left with two choices:
1. Replay that entire brutal last mission and try to not use as many potions and knives etc this time around.
2. Go to youtube to skip this 5 minute fight and watch the ending of the game.

People who breezed through this fight had enough Amber (think mana) to turn invisible etc. Without that, the final fight can be a horrible affair. I went with option #2 out of frustration after making about 8 or so attempts. It was said on the forums that this is how the game makes you be more careful and not wasteful in the previous level to “show off your skill” but letting you get stuck like this is a big negative for me.

CONCLUSION

Ok so is the game worth it? It may sound from all the above that I really didn’t like the game that much but honestly it’s a great game. It’s a great game especially if you play in a way that you sneak by and don’t fight. The story and voice acting is great and the world is beautifully rendered. I found the ending satisfying, even though I had to watch it on youtube =(.
For perfectionists out there, there are challenges to collect coins and to find hidden artifacts. For 32 bucks I got 23 hours of gameplay and I did very few actual extras which could have given me a few more hours. The game is well worth it, even with the caveats listed above.
My score is 8/10.

E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy isn't for everyone. It's not even for most people. E.Y.E. feels like a source mod that exploded out of control. Some parts are good, some parts are bad, some parts are inoffensively meh.
The Bad:
It was originally written in French and translated poorly to english. Would be a minor issue if the plot of the story wasn't a cyberpunk adventure multiple thousands of years in the future.
E.Y.E explains maybe 20% of what there is to do and how you can do it. Even after watching the 20 hastily thrown together tutorial videos you'll probably be confused.
2-3 Researches cost money but have literally no effect.
You have no idea what you're doing on your first 4 character creations or so before you understand the wonders of 3 MetaStreum DNA's and randomizing until all stats are green/yellow.
E.Y.E. Is VERY beginner unfriendly and probably turned a lot of people off with its rough presentation.
The ability "honeycomb" menu routinely glitches and drops what abilities you had mapped between loading levels. Mostly a non issue but can be annoying.
Background FX can be nothing in some levels. In one area the only real background noise is a loop of far away guns popping shots off at one another. In a different area it's just very quiet dripping in a sewer. It's somewhat low effort sounding.
I would recommend always playing with classic UI. Full UI seems to remove certain important hud elements and add.. just weird stuff. If I recall correctly Full UI adds a mystical Buddha to the bottom left of your screen that, as far as I know, doesn't convey anything. It could be karma? 40 hours in to E.Y.E and I still don't know.
The Meh:
It was originally written in French and translated poorly to english.
E.Y.E. is based off of a tabletop board game, AVA or something of that nature. This is quite apparent when looking at the Research, Stats, and Implants screens. They're quite a bit more in depth than almost every other video game, but also hardly explained in the slightest. May or may not be your cup of tea.
The backstory, of which there are seemingly twenty terminals at the Headquarters to read from, appears to be ripped sloppily from Warhammer 40k. It's okay but unless you're in the mood for it then it can feel "blah" while reading.
Guns could stand to sound a bit heftier, they feel and sound "light" and not very punchy.
At the higher levels of difficulty any enemy stronger than a grunt typically only has to see you for about a half second before they blow you away. This problem persists long into the upper levels, with my Level 65 (mid-range) Medium reinforced armor warrior being 2-3 shot by an enemy Lieutenant or Master.
Some levels can feel samey or boring. Missions can vary from a wild ride blowing things up and hacking terminals and blasting dudes to.. running around a small map picking up objective items, or running through dark tunnels.
The interact function is mapped to "Enter" instead of "E". But movement is still mapped to WASD. Q and E lean left and right. Best option would be to map one of the buttons on your mouse to "Enter" so you don't have to constantly reach over and hit enter while trying to do things.
The aiming system is click and lock instead of hold to aim. Tap right mouse once to go into aim and it stays that way. Tap it again to either go out of aim or zoom in further (depending on your weapon). This can be annoying for hold to aim shooters like myself.
Top left U.I. is really weird. It somewhat details what's happening but most of the time you're focused on the center of your screen. Really it only conveys 5 messages. "Careful, you're bleeding!" for if you're Hemorrhaging. "You gained brouzoufs" for when you get money. "Your leg is broken" and "My legs are OK" for the state of your legs, and "..."
The Good:
It was originally written in French and translated poorly to english. This is hilarious and zany sometimes, giving you some truly brilliant expletive filled lines about throwing someones head into a vat of acid while you "wear their [EXPLETIVE] moronic face as a party mask.
There are so many amazing gameplay quirks and the freedom to do whatever you want at higher levels is so fun. When you start out you're this weak, underpowered guy with abilities like "Jog at a light pace instead of shamble" and "Jump slgihtly higher than normal". But 50 levels later after you've invested a million Brouzoufs (slang for money) into your cyber legs and you've bumped your agility stat up to 65 and you've done a few researches that increase your agility and running speed, THEN you're this speed demon sprinting down the street at 60 miles an hour, jumping 40 feet into the air, telefragging into a sniper 50 meters away and going invisible so you can hunt down his buddies like the predator.
There are so many ways to play E.Y.E. that it can feel overwhelming. On my first character I went with a typical Shotgun-Hobo. Pistol strapped to my leg and shotgun on my back, I blasted my way through bandits and space federals and aliens and werewolves. After that I decided to experiment. I went for a street samurai, packing nothing but a pistol and a katana that explodes when I hit people with it. Then I went for a stealth cybermancer hacker, setting down sentry guns and deploying drones that orbitted me while I hacked into bank terminals and enemy soldiers alike. Instead of assassinating a high priority target myself, I hacked and hypnotized his henchmen so they would do the dirty work for me.
Art direction. E.Y.E. has some beautiful levels and character design. A run down apartment neighborhood next to a factory, bathed in toxic green fog and home to dozens of bandits and gangsters. A brightly lit city block at night streaked by neon lights of every color, all giving off this dreamlike glow. The arcturus space station, filled with tightly packed hallways that open into large industrial areas, but on the sides and front of the station are these big open-view windows and dropoffs where you can look into the asteroid dotted crimson fade of space.
Lets me lug around a chaingun and mow aliens down. Also lets me telefrag an alien werewolf from another dimension into a bandit. Also lets me naruto clone jutsu 9 copies of myself and command them to run headfirst out onto the mars landscape where a 40 meter tall space demon thing blows them up instantly. Also lets me use Deckers gun from Blade Runner.
Shotguns act like shotguns and are effective beyond 2 meters. Feels very good to blast a bandit to atoms from 25 meters down the road.
E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy is an experience. A real experience. Not "The Order: 1886" where every level is a tube that you walk through and then once in a while you get to "experience" the rocket launcher section or the projectile flamethrower section for 2 minutes. E.Y.E. is an insane mess that I can't in good contience give an A, but isn't anywhere near average or bad enough to give a C, D, or F. Trying to quantify the entire experience under a single letter grade or score out of ten isn't possible really, E.Y.E. took so many ideas and did so many of them meh and so many of them well.
E.Y.E. Divine Cybermancy is a bag of trail mix where the M&M's are replaced with gold pieces and the raisins are replaced with chucks of street asphalt. 9/10 MY LEGS ARE OK

I grabbed this game during the Steam summer sale for about three dollars, and it was well worth the price. That's not a compliment - this game is three dollars worth of fun, now at five times the worthy cost.
It might be more fun if there was an online community, but there isn't, or at least there wasn't when I was playing.
Overall it's a decent game. Fairly fun. The basic idea is that you get to flip, jump, and run around like a normal platformer, with the added bonus of having to fence/fist-fight enemies. Once you kill an enemy, you can start running towards the end goal. If an enemy kills you, HE can run towards the end goal. Whoever dies gets to respawn and try to stop the other from getting there, but the guy running can literally jump over you and keep going. It takes a bit of skill and getting used to, but when you pick up the controls and start really understanding things, you'll get the hang of it.
Again, it's a decent game, it's just not worth fifteen dollars. Maybe if there were more people to play online with, or there were more stages, characters, or weapons, but there's only about four or five stages (if even that many), one type of weapon (not counting hand-to-hand), and there's only the one character (you can't even choose your color). So, all in all, it's just not worth it.
Not many people have this game yet, which dissapoints me. A masterpiece like this should be popular, but what am I to judge? I'm not a critic. I just love games.

As everyone else has said, it is riddled with bugs. If it were an animal, I would put it down. Until they fix the plethora of bugs and conenctivity issues, save your money.
So I'll break down my >2 hours of gameplay before I refunded.
Campaign - I haven't tried single player, but multiplayer campaign is unplayable. The lag between the host and myself was around 1 full second of delay, and obviously, with micro-intensive games, that is unacceptable. I didn't put a lot of time into this mode due to aforementioned issue.
Skirmish - Again, big lag delay. The AI seems to spam out a million buildings, making pretty much the entirety of the map, minus your own base, a giant, cluttered mess. If you play this mode singleplayer, I'd reckon you'd solve the poor latency issue, but the mode in itself just isn't that fun past the intitial 20 minutes of base set up. It needs a lot of AI tweaks and and resource balancing.
The developers noted in game, that you can fix connectivity issues by forwarding ports to your router. It's a headache to do, and I feel like they have essentially made their problem ours. I feel like this game was released too soon, with too many problems. Also, the loading times are absolutely ridiculous. Unless you have this game on an SSD, you will be waiting a very long time to load.
I will leave this review ona  positive note, and say that this game has incredible potential. If the devs fix the connection and balancing issues, and work with the community to make a polished game, I think that it may be worth the $54.99 purchase price.

A initial point is to say that this game is translated over into English. There are many moments when the grammar and wording is awkward. Yet despite that, this game shines in so many ways.
E.Y.E gives us, as a player, a glimpse into an odd dystopian world that leaves you with an odd feeling. The game seems to steep itself in philosophical and psychological undertones (despite at times feel too vague) while allowing for action and moments of quick reaction. I enjoyed the oddity of the characters and the leveling system. I also enjoyed the ability to change my weapons and armor whenever I felt it was necessary. A major flaw in the level system I found however, was through the usage of sniper rifles. As long as you make headshots with a sniper rifle; you could rake in all the exp as quickly as possible. I played this game solo and co-op. My friends and I found that I could level 3 times before my friends would level once, if I used a sniper rifle. We had to ban the sniper rifle in our co-op games due to insane level gaps. This brings me to the second issue – the scripting for co-op. When my friends and I decided to co-op, we would have to spend 30mins attempting to connect to each other as we opened ports and synchronized via Hamachi or steam.
Despite these flaws, I still highly recommend this game. I would love an E.Y.E 2 in a new engine. This game has potential and mechanics that are not often used. If you have a sci-fi, dystopian, psychic itch; look no further than this game! It has it all!

I've spent entirely too much time playing this game. Sure, it's only three hours, but when you consider that each match is around 3 minutes at the most, and 30 seconds at the least, it becomes clear how addicting and fun this game really is.
You play a small stick man. Your opponent is also a small stick man. You must be the human sacrifice to the worm god Nidhogg before your opponent. To do this, you must win fencing rounds in order to gain camera control. You keep camera control until you are killed. The advantage of having camera control is that you're able to just run by your opponent, allowing very skilled players to win a round in well under a minute.
While not exactly "enthralling", it's easily one of my favorite party games that I own due to the bracket system it offers for tournament play. The game is easy enough for my older family members who don't play, and simple enough that talent sometimes isn't enough. With four different maps to choose from, and all sorts of play styles to learn, Nidhogg is a good time for all sorts.
Should you get it? If you love playing games with your friends, don't waste any time at all in snatching up this little gem. What it lacks in graphical content it makes up for in exciting gameplay, and a genuinely good time. I'm also a big fan of one-off games that you can play while waiting for something to finish cooking, or whatever, and this is quick enough to pick up and put down in an instant. I HIGHLY recommend this very fun title.
EDIT: Currently the game sits at 15 bucks. That's kind of ludicrous. While extremely fun, I wouldn't say it's worth quite that much. Perhaps wait for a sale.

Hmm, this was a tough one to recommend. Why? There was so much to it that I found to be attributing to being boring. I had to look up how to achieve each route, and as I went through each, I realized that you don't make very many decisions at all. In fact, there is only like 6 major decisions (Depending on the previous decisions you have made) I like a visual novel where you make a lot of decisions, regardless of how much plot you have. Also, the characters felt very rigid with their movements and facial expressions a lot during the scenes where people were talking to each other in a non-special scene. It was just weird. Also, it may be just the fact that I am new to visual novels, but I felt that the pacing was very...slow. That could just be the fact that very few decisions were made, but still. Now, I did actually enjoy the hell out of this at times. I am semi-new to visual novels and gameplay, but a lot of times, this had very realistic scenes of the glider flying in the air, etc. The art was amazing, and I love animes and visual novels that strive to create vivid imagery and lighting. It was phenominal. For the sound, the music was fairly limited in its range, but the sound effects made were very well done, if you ask me. I would give this a solid 6/10, not because it is mediocre, but because there are a lot of elements to a game/visual novel that need to be adjusted in order to make the audience a bit more interested in the story, even with a good soundtrack, where this one had like 1 really good song. That was the opening song in the main menu. I wanted to seriously play this and be enthralled, and to some degree, I was.
*Don't be too harsh. I am new to making reviews on here*

Unless there are a lot of subtleties to Cricket that this game misses and I'm just unaware of, Cricket Captain 2015 deserves far better than a 'mixed' review level.
I knew next to nothing about Cricket, but I do play a lot of sports management sims. I don't think there's a major game of that genre that I haven't played, and this seems like one of the better ones. The in-game graphics are outstanding for a management sim, just compare it to OOTP and FM. The management isn't as deep as those two games, of course, but it's good enough to satisfy me.
What I really like about CC 2015 is the fog of war regarding players. You don't have visible attribute settings that tell you exactly how good a player is. You get told what his tendencies are and what his stats are, and you work out from there if he'll be a fit for you or not. If a player is performing crap, you think, well, is he just unlucky? Am I using him wrong? Or is he actually crap? The player attributes make most management games easy to win; this game on the other hand is a great challenge.
In OOTP there are a sizable minority of us who play using 'stats only', where we turn attributes off and evaluate players based on performance. If you're an OOTP player who enjoys that style, you'll love this. I'm very happy with this purchase.

This is a wonderful cricket simulation game - hands down the best I've ever played.  I think I've sunk something like 400 hours into this game and its 2014 predecessor, more than any other game I own on steam.
This game has two weaknesses that I think account for most of the negative reviews on steam.  Its true that this game lacks some of the wider elements of sports management that other high profile titles have.  Its strength is its match engine though, which performs well across all forms of the game (one dayers, tests and T20s) and can still give the occassional surprise. Seriously, I've played this game for 400 hours plus, and every game is still a nailbiter.
The other weakness is the fact that the game is evolving only slowly - I think most of the negative reviews on steam relate to disappointment from people who have bought previous editions and were hoping for more from the latest.  That seems to be true to a degree, but doesnt change the fact that this is a great cricket management game.  Its also the case that the game is developed by a very small team - I imagine it cant be easy to make a living out of a game like this.  So for me I'm happy to pay for updates to keep the game moving forward.
If you love cricket, do yourself a favour and buy this game.

When this game was released I thought it seemed pretty fun, but I couldn't picture myself buying it, mostly because of Ubisoft. But when I saw it is just 4 euros on the sales I just felt the urge to grab it. What I made out of it is simply that it is purely 2.5 gb of pure fun. The game mechanics are addicting, the graphics and aesthetics are neat and the product is top notch. In a few words, it is like agario but upgraded, the "big eats small" formula. The thing is Reflections is just a Ubisoft Studio, not ubisoft itself, as it is carefully stated and for a good reason on the product page. The developers actually seem to take good care of the game and they haven't inculded uplay as compulsory. So, all in all it is an amazing game that deserves way more recognition. The drawbacks that could be proven to be  hindrances to some though are the following: 1) First and foremost is the low population and it is not the game's fault. The only way to get fixed is by getting more players in the game. 2) Peer to peer connection, which is considered by many as a disadvantage. To be honest though, I didn't deal with any problem with the connectivity, nor did I notice any latency issue, not to mention that the peer to peer connection ensures that you can always play the game despite the population, which as was stated is pretty low. In case the game fails to make any substantial profit, the dedicated servers would had to be shut down and you would had wasted your money. 3) The lack of leaderboards/ ranking system/competitive scene/ variety of game modes, which is also to be expected since the population is numbered. Thus, it is essential to mention that if you intend to play with your friends, you must set up a private match and play by yourselves.4) Kind of bad optimization considering you cannot run it on stable 60 fps on max with a gtx 1060 gb, an i5 6500 and 16 gb of ddr4 ram, which is far more than the recommended strrings. All in all, all the problems line with the minimal playerbase. Even in the game's relatively early state, its value outshines the rest, which can nonetheless be fixed if more people gather. So in conclusion, is the game worth 4 euros? Definitely. Do I see potential in the game and willing developers. Yes, they already proved it by releasing new maps already, and there is actually a progression system with cosmetics to back that up. Should I worry about the restricted amount of players? Yes, since you simply cannot play alone, but if you actually buy it with 4 friends then you are set. Also, the more people get the game, the better for the experience. All it takes is 6 players more or less to get the full experience anyway. All of that said, if you can afford spending that relatively small amount comparing it with the prices of other games and considering its quality, it is a surefire yes, undoubtely.
