I used to play a lot of tabletop 40K, and after playing the first Dawn of War a few years ago I was looking forward to another instalment. I wish I hadn't bothered: stabbing myself in both eyes with sporks while gargling lukewarm badger diarrhea would have been a much more enjoyable and productive use of my time. Unfortunately I can't get a refund as I put more than 2 hours into Last Stand mode before finding out that the rest of the game was completely broken, so I'm leaving this review instead in the hope that nobody else will make the same mistake.
When I finally got around to loading up a Private Multiplayer game, I selected game options, invited a mate to play with and the game crashed. So I tried again, and it crashed. And again, and it crashed. A trip to Google later and someone said the only way they managed to get it to work at all was by manually selecting the races of all the CPU players, as leaving any of them on random meant - you guessed it - the game crashed. Colour me stunned.
When I finally got into a game, I discovered that it was basically Dawn of War I adapted for short attention spans and low IQs. Base building? Gone. Resource management? Simplified to the point of pointlessness. Variety? You get 5 races to choose from, with the rest gated off behind so many pieces of DLC it would make EA say "Hang on a minute, don't you think this is a bit of a rip-off?"
I'm amused to note that apparently Dawn of War III will re-introduce some of the game mechanics that were removed. This is about as close as a game developer comes to admitting fault, but I've learned my lesson and I won't be buying it; I'll be saving my money for sporks and badger laxatives.

This game had potential. I loved dawn of war, dawn of war dark crusade, and dawn of war soulstorm but this isnt the same. The gameplay is completely different. I will split this between three segments.
Campaign: I enjoy the campaign. You get 4 squad slots and all 5 squads and you choose what you want. the squads include, commander, scout, devistators, tactical, and assault. The squads are nice (not the assault it isnt that great). And you get to add armor and weapons to them like the campaign of dark crusade and soulstorm. The game also has a cover based mechanic that is weird and doesnt work 100% of the time.
skermish/online: I loved the custom games in the first games but this game doesn't do that well. Back in those games you would build bases and choose what buildings go where and I loved that. This game doesnt have that it is just one base with few troop choices in it. You dont make multiple bases either just the one. The AI difficulty for custom games has been ramped up to the point where it's now a brick wall so now it kinda sucks. I would skip it if I were you.
Last stand: THIS IS THE KNEES OF THE BEES. I love last stand. Last stand is a wave survival game. There are three players and they choose a character. There are 5 factions and each faction has three characters. Each one has abilities and weapons others do not have. Just like the campaign you can add wargear to your character. You get wargear by leveling up. I hope there is terminator armor for the space marine force commander for last stand because it would be just broken. Speaking of broken use the force commander and spam blinding grenades by the time the enemies are no longer stunned, you got your grenades back.
In conclusion if you want a squad based cover shooter I would suggest waiting for a sale to pick it up. But if you are wanting a dawn of war RTS strategy game then go to the originals or wait for dawn of war 3. I picked this game up for $4 and i have to say it is worth $4 no more than $7.

I had a blast playing this and chaos rising expansion. I see many complaining of thew lack of basebuilding and that you only control a few number of soldiers/squads. Well in my opinon i find this type of strategy to be more true to Space Marine nature. You get a few battle deciding squads instead of a whole army. You deep strike into the heart of the enemy or to key areas instead of spending whole hours gathering resources and training an army. The maps are fairly open for you to not take same route every playthrough and with the abilities of your squads you can sneak around or massacre entire areas. It includes a skillbuilding and gearequipping system that is beating some rpgs. You get only enough skills to max out 2/4 skill trees so you need to think about the points you spend and how you spend them reflects in how you play the game. Makes the replay value good, if you want to respec your squads for a different playstyle. Devestators with missile launchers and tactical armor - flamers and dreadnaught armor, Tactical and Assualt squads with range weapons or melee weapons. With chaos rising you get the addition of corruption points with bonuses for both currupted and pure squads. I would say its worth to add rpg tags for this game. Also it is definatly worth picking up on sale.
To answer one reviewer that said that he get oneshotted in bossfights, well thats for its a tactical game, you need to keep your squads positioned well, move them if targeted and learn when to use your abilities. Also sometimes its not best idea to equip the item with best stats, for your abilities may not have been set for that item.
If you take the time to learn the game, it wont take long until you get 5/5/5 rating after a mission and have fun doing it.

Epic Tavern is a fun little game with a novel concept. It's a bit of a mashup between an RPG crossed with a tavern simulator. Each round consists of tending to the needs of travelers passing through your establishment. You can ply them with booze and chow to get them to open up with stories. Does pretty much what you expect out of a stealth game and has impressively dramatic vertical level designs.
My biggest issue with S:MoS is that, while Dishonored had amazing worldbuilding and loads of collectible secrets, and Thief was *all* about going off the beaten path to hunt for loot, S:MoS gives you almost no incentive to  explore the levels besides architectural appreciation and obsessive-compulsive token hunting (which gives far too low a reward for such a tedious challenge). So while the levels are impressively designed, traversing them sometimes feels more like overcoming a bare-bones challenge than exploring a developed world. This is more visible in the obligatory interior/underground/cavernous levels, where the vertical level design isn't as prominent or as impressive. While I still enjoy the challenge, I wish there had been more to discover in the nooks and crannies of the game.

Epic Tavern is a tavern-managament simulator with great RPG elements, developed by Hyperkinetic Studios, and i need to say, I’ve been waiting a game like this for a long time.
First, i need to say the athmosphere is awesome. As a fan of medieval-RPG’s and taverns/inns, i totally lost myself in it. Musics and sound effects are amazingly good.
Gameplay is fun, you are a tavern master, and serve to your patrons. You also can hire people to your party, and go to adventures with them. At the beggining, you’ll have limit on your roaster, but you can increase the number of people you hired by leveling up your Tavern. Also you can level up the people’s skills you hired,
Each game day, an amount of AP becomes available to you. You can spend AP’s by talking to patrons, serving them, etc. By the way talking to patrons is the only way to receive quests, so it’s pretty important.
There are several types of quests, like Story and Tavern and they’re all text-based. Basically, story quests helps you to go further in the story, and tavern quests helps you to expand your tavern, etc.
Overall, Epic Tavern is great for the medieval rpg fans like myself, game is still on Early Access, so there are some minor bugs, but devs working hard on fixing them. Don’t hesitate and go for it!

Build your base, defend it against the Titans, explore new stuff in the tech tree and then: do it all over again in the next challenging level of Revenge Of The Titans. It is as simple as that! But it is also very addictive gameplay. By now I have clocked in more than 50 hours ingame, more than I can say of other (more mainstream) titles. The concept of tower defense games may sound simple to you, but make no mistake, the learning curve for this game can be steep sometimes. At least, you can always go back a few levels and experiment with other items in your tech tree and then spend countless hours trying new tactics with different weapons. However, should you be stuck on a particular level, you can always ask around in the steam forums, the developers are very active there and give excellent insight into the game mechanics (e.g. why you should upgrade a turret, how to maximize profits from mining crystals, etc.). To cut a long story short: I love this game!

To start off, I just wanted to say sorry to JForce Ty and his team for my original review I felt was very lackluster since i had not booted up the game for a little over a year.
Murder Miners is a FPS game styled like minecraft with guns and weapons to your disposal. After spending around a half hour playing the game after not booting it up in a year, I was suprised on how nastolgic it felt. The gameplay reminds me of some of the early HALO games but it's styled like minecraft. I have plenty of hours spend on games from the HALO franchise (1863 hours across all games) and a decent amount of time played on minecraft (237 hours) so this game actually brought back alot of memories. I love this game and I can't wait until Murder Miners X is released. I have a few suggestions on what to add to the game or something to save for Murder Miners X.
1. Create A Class
This would include a variety of perks and weapons and possibly weapon skins.
2. Interactive envorments
Buttons, Switches, Levers you name it, it would be a nice additon to the game.
3. FOV slider
I love to change my FOV in FPS games and while playing Murder Miners, I really wish it was there.
4. Third Person
I know third person is already on the helicopter and the hover bike but maybe a option you could add before you start a match in this game to spice things up a bit?
Overall, I think Murder Miners was a good purchase. For the price it is, gather some of your friends and sit down and play a game or two and you'll have tons of fun.

Nidhogg is not bad at all in terms of gameplay. I won’t go into much detail because the trailers and such pretty much show what it's about, but its damn fun to play. The combat has a lot of options and things going for it and nicely juggles both complexity and ease of learning. The music and visuals match and mesh with the feel of the combat excellently. I can easily see how co-op can be a blast with friends, or the tourney potential.
So why is this not recommended? Because the devs cared more about the game’s style, raw gameplay, and media hype then its long-term substance or support. You’re playing this game and having a lot of fun, and then before you even hit the one hour mark you find yourself thinking “that’s it?” and then it’s all downhill from there. Singleplayer consists of you fighting a dozen or two progressively harder AI opponents, however the stages start looping after opponent four. Yep, only four stages. There’s no story to speak of or even an attempt at one, and once you’re done with it you’re left with nearly nothing else to do with the game. Multiplayer is dead, D-E-A-D. Its features are minimal and in terms of functionality the MP barely worked when the game came out, and then because they never fixed it people gave up on it entirely so there’s no one playing.
This game deserved more support and more features and updates from a solid company. But because it didn’t get that and most likely won’t ever, I am sorry to say that charging $15 for this is broad daylight robbery and I cannot recommend it. Only buy this if it’s on sale, and with the understanding that outside of being a weekend distraction or occasional hour of fun with a friend this game has no value.

As far as Metroidvania genre is concerned, I'd say this is my single absolute favorite game. And that is statement not to be taken lightly, given fact that I played the most prominent examples, or should I say namesakes like ever satysfying Order of Ecclesia. Valdis Story supplies the player with rich story arc to play through using 4 very distinct characters. Both personality and gameplay wise.
Combat is definetly one of the strongest points of VS. It feels extremely fast, visceral and satysfying when you manage to rack up higher and higher combo count, whilst evading incoming enemy attacks. Furthermore, each character can unlock multiple different weapons to utilize. Important note: there is a finite amount of resources per playthrough, so it is wise to choose your biggest favorite and stick with it for the remainder of campaign. Fortunately, any weapons you manage to unlock during your adventure, will be availabe from the very start of your next game.
Final note, many issues mentioned in some of the older reviews have long since been resolved. For example double jump ability is not tied to single magic spell, rather it simple and intuitive passive upgrade to your classical jump. Also most of the game difficulty levels do not feature build-in "timer until game over". You are free to play in such hardcore way if you so choose. Just pick Goibniu mode and be ready for no mercy mode.
I wholeheartedly recommend Valdis Story, and encourage anyone interested to play it to absolute completion.

Valdis Story is a game with a bit of a misleading store page.
Not in the sense of No Man's Sky trying to show off things it doesn't have. But it actually undersells itself.
It says assume the role of Wyatt, and then later says that there's two characters to play as. There's actually 4 and they're all unique in their own way, as well as allowing you to play those said 4 characters in a variety of ways. It also doesn't mention the arena or challenge mode.
That being said, it has amazing combat, story, and music, and quite a bit of replayability.
The combat is very solid and heavy, but not slow. Everything you do in combat feels very responsive and rewarding. Hitting an enemy feels like hitting an enemy. Unlike some other games that are significantly too fluid to the point where you're just a river of damage and physics need not apply other than your own inputs.
This means you need to plan out and adjust your style in order to overcome different challenges. Maybe one boss is better faced with something that can give you some breathing room, or another requires you to be able to time your skill cancels correctly.
The story is very interesting, and if you want to know more than what the game tells you through normal play, there's the lore tomes on top of that. And they're different for each character. Giving you insight on the world itself instead of just the current events unfolding. I would love to say more but I fear anything else may be viewed as a spoiler.
The music. It's one of the few games I bothered to go and buy the soundtrack for. Even though it's less accessable than others seeing how the soundtrack is not available on Steam. It's great, I love it.
Overall, this is one of my favourite games on Steam. And it's not even that expensive. I would've paid at least $10 more for it.

This little gem of a game came to me from steam recommendations when it the recommendations system was in its infancy.
What the game lacks in dialogue and sound effects it makes up for in spades with literally everything else. Enemy variety, good bosses, combat with a high mastery curve and a good difficulty curve to match it, a very good magic system, story, environments, music, you name it.
The enemy variety is self explanatory, and I'm not going to get into "what makes a boss good" here, but single player games with high mastery curves are very very hard to come by.
The game has a mechanic where you upgrade a cancel, progressively getting more uses of it as the game goes on. The cancel launches you to the ground if you're in the air, and can be used to quickly move horizontally once on the ground. It also can be used without moving. It cancels whatever animation the character is currently doing, allowing you to extend combos by cancelling right after the last move in the combo and restarting the combo. This can extend to spells, and as you get more uses of the cancel, your options in fights get larger and larger.
And the game isn't too harsh on you starting out. It really eases you into the skill cancel. The first boss is pretty tough but he forces you to learn a bunch of stuff about the combat.
The sound effects can be annoying and get reused too often, and the dialogue can be kinda contrived at times. The backer NPCs especially are kinda cringy.
But overall, this is a fantastic action game, and definitely a pickup for anyone looking for a challenge.

So far I've only played an hour but I know I'll finish this game because it's too fun. If you're into the whole strategy/hacking aspect of Watch Dogs where you control everything within your vicinity to your advantage, you'll probably enjoy this game. Unlike Watch Dogs, it executes it perfectly and all in the form of a 2D pixel-art indie game. The game gets more challenging and as you progress you have to put more thought to each level. The game also has a sort of "process of elimination" aspect to it like Hotline Miami, where you have to keep dying in order to figure out the best way through the level. For a game I got on sale for less than a dollar this really is one of the most satisfying games I've played in a while.

Rising world can be described as Minecraft, but the world isn't made of blocks. There are not any monsters in it, and no ranged weapons, but animals give a good way for some melee combat if you're looking for that. Hunger and thirst work great. The devs are very supportive and constantly working to improve this already amazing game. Progression in the game is long but rewarding, allowing you to create explosives, and a metal detector to help you find sulfur to make more explosives, and even save your castle on a blueprint for the price of one gold bar, giving you the ability to build it anywhere you want, even in other worlds. And, if you don't feel like building your own city, you can find some custom blueprints on the internet, and build them in your world! The only thing I have against this game is that it's too easy in survival mode. once you find water you can easily set up there, put shelter, and the second you get iron you can make a sickle and hoe and start a farm, giving you an endless source of food and water.
EDIT: a lot of people have been complaining about the 'lack of updates', and, while I can see where they are coming from, they don't realize that the devs are looking for quality and not quantity. also, they think this game is going to be a pure survival game, which is not the case. they are planning on improving survival, but it is still mostly a building game atm. keep this in mind when buying Rising World.
Overall, Rising World is great if you're looking for a relaxing survival game or just to build a fortress.

The Men of War series of games are the exact same game, with different units and maps. There is no real difference between them.  So it doesn't realy matter which one you get. I have played All of them several times, including vietnam and assault squad 2. HOWEVER when you have purchased one title, please trim your fingernails and ductape them, otherwise you risk scratching your own face of, out of frustration over this game.
First to the things that this game does right:
+ Direct control of a unit - To be able to take control of a unit is fun, efficient and a nice feature that enables players who are not into RTS to accualy participate in the game as a coop unit.
+ Sounds and graphic - This game feels very much like a real warzone, the sounds, explosions, fire, destruction of terrain and especialy the vehicles are excellent and there realy is no title quite like it.
+ Vehicle and hit zones - All vehicles have different vulnerability at different parts of it (like in WOT). Different parts of the vehicle can be disabled and will effect the performance of it depending on which part. For example, take out the tracks = no movement, damage turret = turret can't turn (cannon can still fire)
+ Mission diversity - Im very impressed with the engine, because the very same engine that runs the small stealth missions, is also handeling the huge battles. The mission have a huge variety which enables all the titles of men of war to be almost equaly enjoyable.
Now to the bad things <:,(
- THE STUPID♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ AI! - This is by far the worst downside of this game, all positive aspects of this game is dwarfed by this horrible ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ babylike thing. It doesn't take long to realise that your units will almost NEVER complete the most simple of orders. so multiple duplications of the same orders have to be issued for them to complete one. Im not talking about advanced orders here like minelaying or rearming. Im talking about simple attack, movement orders. They will also refuse to do some orders completely and some of the assigned orders have been out of order (spread out which has been avalible for all titles) since the very first title, nothing accualy happens when you push the assigned key. Medics don't heal unless clicking every single unit that has been downed. the list goes on and on and ON!
Men of War has by far the worst AI I have ever seen in any game in my entire life (and I played games for more than 25 years).
- Too advanced controls - The ability to control every unit of this game to such detailness as in this game is a double edged sword. To deal with the stupid AI, it is necessary to have advanced controls. However it also gives the game a very hard learningcurve. and a very simple misstake with handeling your units can cost you the victory in an entire game, both multiplayer and singleplayer.
- Optimisation - This game despite haveing an old engine tends to cramp up when too much things are happening at the same time in one screen. I do believe the reason for most singleplayer missions to be small is due to this game not being optimized. The physics enginee gets overheated quickly when too much is happening at the same time, this combined with freecamera rotation can make it possible to crash the game if you tilt it too much so it reavels to great of an area of the map.

Awesome game!

First half of the game is entertaining, then you have to play through the same levels again, backwards.
Then it gets even less fun, as you go through a series of encounters with the "boss" - which is to say you come out of a cutscene, have a couple seconds to react, or die.  Every time you run into him, you go through this "fun" sequence.
No relevance to your sneaking or killing skills you have built up playing this game.  It all comes down to "react or die".
WORST boss encounters I've encountered in a long time.   I finally gave up on the final (i think) encounter and deleted the game.   I honestly don't care enough to go through more of these react-or-die scenes.

i started with construct 2 a few months back in my free time, its so EASY no coding required! you just have to understand basic logic and you will come a long way, don't start with big things at first try some small things in the beginning. if you don't know how to make something try and search it, construct 2 has a big community that will help each other out. i will definitely buy a licence in the near future!
